title: Grid and Road Expressions Are Complementary for Trajectory Representation Learning

problem.claim: Trajectory representation learning maps trajectories to vectors for downstream tasks.

gap.claim: Existing methods use either grid trajectories or road trajectories, leaving their complementary region, location, road-structure, and movement-regularity information jointly underused.

contributions.claim: GREEN jointly uses grid and road trajectory expressions for trajectory representation learning.

GREEN transforms raw GPS trajectories into grid and road trajectories, uses tailored encoders, aligns them with contrastive and masked-language-model losses, and fuses their outputs with a cross-attention dual-modal interactor.
The authors report that code and data are available.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe GREEN as a novel multimodal trajectory representation learning method.

author_reported_evidence.claim: GREEN was compared with 7 state-of-the-art trajectory representation learning methods on 3 downstream tasks.
The authors report that GREEN consistently outperformed all baselines and improved the accuracy of the best-performing baseline by an average of 15.99%.

narrative_sequence.summary: Trajectory representation learning produces vector representations for downstream tasks.
Existing approaches separately use grid or road trajectories, although the two representations provide complementary information.
GREEN builds grid and road trajectories, encodes them separately, aligns the encoders with two losses, and fuses them through cross-attention.
The authors report comparisons against 7 baselines across 3 downstream tasks, with an average 15.99% improvement over the strongest baseline.
Code and data are reported as available.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the downstream tasks, datasets, baseline identities, or evaluation protocol.
The abstract does not provide implementation details, computational costs, or ablation results.
